_meta.purpose: Grounded symptom->fix knowledge dictated by Teddy (owner/master tech). Feeds the Ant customer chat, tech diagnostic assist, and brand/symptom web pages. Every entry is a real, common repair TN Appliance does. 'easy' = fast, affordable, high-margin. 'smarthq' = on newer GE we read it via SmartHQ factory diagnostics.
_meta.rules: Never quote a part number to a customer. Warranty jobs never hit a payment screen. Use this to lead with the exact symptom the customer describes, then the honest fix.

entries.likely_cause: linear compressor failure
entries.fix: This is our signature repair — we're sealed-system certified and swap LG compressors all the time, so it's a fast, in-and-out job done right, not a week-long runaround. We check the LG 10-year limited compressor-part warranty FIRST; if it's covered you mostly pay labor. Recover, braze in the new compressor, pull a deep vacuum, recharge, back to cooling.
entries.note: Our brag-worthy specialty — the fastest, most-trusted LG compressor swap around. Lead with speed + sealed-system certified (the moat most independents can't clear) + warranty-first (the money-saver and trust-builder). Warranty companies dispatch these to us.

entries.likely_cause: ice maker assembly, water inlet valve, or frozen line
entries.fix: Replace ice maker assembly / inlet valve.

entries.likely_cause: drain pump (the LG front-load weak spot) — coin/hairpin caught or worn pump
entries.fix: Clear or replace the drain pump. Cheap, fast fix — the drain pump is LG's weak link but easy to service.
entries.note: LG front-loaders are the best out there per Teddy — the drain pump is the one weak spot ('weaker than a wet paper towel'). New or old we'd buy one.

entries.likely_cause: worn tub bearing (older front-loaders)
entries.fix: On older LG front-loaders a worn tub bearing gets loud/rough — a bigger job. Give the honest repair-vs-replace call, especially if control boards are hard to source on the older unit.
entries.note: The two older-LG caveats: bad bearings + hard-to-find boards. Otherwise a great washer.

entries.likely_cause: heating element (older LG dryers)
entries.fix: Replace the heating element and clear the vent so it lasts. LG dryers are genuinely good — worth fixing.
entries.note: LG dryers hold up well. Older wear items = heater + drum rollers.

entries.likely_cause: worn drum wheels / rollers
entries.fix: Replace the drum rollers — the newer LG rollers cost a bit more but bring it back to smooth and quiet. Worth it.
entries.note: Newer LG dryer rollers are pricier but worth having. Good dryers.

entries.likely_cause: user interface (control panel) OR the door not registering as closed at the door switch
entries.fix: Check the simple thing first — a lot of LG 'won't start' calls are just the door not being recognized as latched (adjust so the door switch engages). If it's the panel, replace the UI.
entries.note: INTERNAL TRICK: on LG dishwashers that won't start, gently bend the top of the door/tub down a touch so the door switch recognizes the door as closed — fixes many 'dead' units before any board. Do NOT publish the trick on customer pages. The other common LG dishwasher failure is the UI panel.

entries.likely_cause: repair-vs-replace / buying judgment
entries.fix: LG's laundry is the best out there right now — a front-load washer or dryer is a yes, worth fixing (older caveats: bearings + hard-to-find boards; the drain pump is the weak spot). The kitchen we'd pass on — beautiful fridges but linear-compressor risk, and we're neutral on the ranges/dishwashers. Send a video + model # for the honest read.
entries.note: Teddy's LG take: BEST laundry out there (washers + dryers, yes); PASS on the kitchen (fridge = compressor risk, stove/dishwasher = indifferent).

entries.likely_cause: drain pump clogged (coin/hairpin/lint) or worn
entries.fix: Clear or replace drain pump; check drain hose.

entries.likely_cause: worn suspension rods, bad shock, or balance sensor
entries.fix: Replace suspension/shock; recalibrate.

entries.likely_cause: French-door ice maker frost-up (airflow + seal)
entries.fix: Fix root cause (airflow/seal) and install improved-revision module so it stays fixed. Do NOT just swap the module.
entries.note: Our Samsung specialty — the fastest icemaker on the market and the FIRST direct-evaporator design (ahead of its time, so it's bound to have quirks). We respect the tech; we just know its weak spot. Most shops swap the module and it fails again — we fix the airflow/frost root cause.

entries.likely_cause: defrost system or frosted evaporator choking airflow
entries.fix: Defrost repair (heater/sensor/control). Not a dead compressor = affordable.

entries.likely_cause: evaporator fan hitting ice buildup behind back panel
entries.fix: Clear ice, fix root cause, replace fan if damaged.

entries.likely_cause: worn idler pulley (and often drum rollers)
entries.fix: Replace the idler pulley / rollers — a common wear part on Samsung dryers. Cheap, fast, runs quiet again the same visit.
entries.note: Samsung is an electronics company first — the mechanical wear parts (idler pulley, rollers) are the weak spot. Almost always worth fixing.

entries.likely_cause: heating element (or a blown thermal fuse behind a clogged vent)
entries.fix: Replace the heating element and clear the vent so the thermal fuse doesn't blow again. Confirm the fuse/thermostats too.
entries.note: The other common Samsung dryer failure — the wear parts an electronics maker underbuilds. Always clear the vent so it lasts.

entries.likely_cause: touch panel (touchpad) failure — the weak point on Samsung ranges
entries.fix: Diagnose the touch panel vs the control board — on Samsung it's usually the touchpad, not the whole control. Replace the failed part instead of throwing boards at it.
entries.note: Samsung range weak spot is the touchpad. Confirm touchpad vs main control before ordering.

entries.likely_cause: worn suspension rods or tired balance ring
entries.fix: Replace suspension/balance ring.
entries.note: Whirlpools are almost always worth fixing.

entries.likely_cause: drain pump clogged or worn
entries.fix: Clear/replace pump; check hose.

entries.likely_cause: main control board fault
entries.fix: Replace main control board.

entries.likely_cause: repair-vs-replace judgment call
entries.fix: Older Whirlpool-family units (incl. Maytag, KitchenAid, Amana) are workhorses — cheap parts, almost always worth fixing, they'll outlive us all. On the NEWEST models we watch for wiring weaknesses, and a few of the newest fridges aren't worth the repair. Send a video + model # and a real tech gives you the honest read. Their dryers are the industry standard — those we fix all day.
entries.note: Teddy's honest Whirlpool take: old = buy-it-for-life, new = wiring weaknesses + some newest fridges not worth fixing. Maytag has been Whirlpool-built ~10 yrs; KitchenAid + Amana = same family. Dryers = industry standard. Teddy runs Whirlpool at home.

entries.likely_cause: repair-vs-replace judgment call
entries.fix: Maytag has been built by Whirlpool for ~10 years — same platforms, parts, and repair playbook. Rugged and highly repairable, older units outlive us all, dryers are the industry standard. Send a video + model # for the honest read on yours.
entries.note: Maytag = Whirlpool family. Same honest read as Whirlpool: old worth fixing, newest watch the wiring.

entries.likely_cause: defrost system or stuck air damper starving fresh-food airflow
entries.fix: Defrost/damper repair. Affordable, not a dead compressor.
entries.note: Our GE specialty.

entries.likely_cause: condenser fan, main control, or sealed system/compressor
entries.fix: Run diagnostics; honest repair-vs-replace.

entries.likely_cause: water inlet valve, stuck float/float switch, or tripped flood-float
entries.fix: Replace/reset the fill path.

entries.likely_cause: blown thermal fuse, failed door latch/switch, or main control
entries.fix: Replace the failed component.

entries.likely_cause: drain pump clogged or worn
entries.fix: Clear/replace pump.

entries.likely_cause: suspension rods, shift actuator, or hall sensor
entries.fix: Replace suspension/actuator.

entries.likely_cause: heating element (electric) / igniter (gas) / blown thermal fuse
entries.fix: Replace element/igniter/fuse; clear the vent so the fuse doesn't blow again.

entries.likely_cause: belt, idler pulley, or drum rollers
entries.fix: Replace belt/idler/rollers.

entries.likely_cause: worn igniter or dirty/misaligned burner cap
entries.fix: Replace igniter / clean-align cap.

entries.likely_cause: bake element (electric) or oven igniter (gas), or temp sensor
entries.fix: Replace element/igniter/sensor.

entries.likely_cause: n/a
entries.fix: On newer GE, connect via SmartHQ to read every stored error code and run factory diagnostic tests for an exact diagnosis before opening a panel.
entries.note: Our GE moat. Most independents can't do this.

entries.likely_cause: user interface (touch panel) or main control board — the known GE dishwasher weak spot
entries.fix: Diagnose UI panel vs control board (on newer GE, read it via SmartHQ) and replace the failed one — a targeted, worth-it fix, not a whole-machine replacement.
entries.note: GE dishwashers are genuinely good machines but the common failure is the UI / control board. Teddy runs one at home. Confirm panel vs board before ordering.

entries.likely_cause: control board / touch panel — GE dryer weak spot (poor button design)
entries.fix: Diagnose the control board / touch membrane and fix the actual fault instead of throwing parts at it. On newer GE, SmartHQ helps.
entries.note: GE dryers are a poor design, especially the buttons. Honest, but we fix them.

entries.likely_cause: GE all-in-one washer/dryer combo — poor repairability
entries.fix: Heads up: the GE all-in-one combo was a neat idea but it's NOT repair-friendly, and it's not a cheap fix. Get the honest repair-vs-replace read (video + model #) before sinking money in.
entries.note: Warn on the GE all-in-one combo: hard to service, expensive fixes. Set expectations honestly up front.

entries.likely_cause: repair-vs-replace judgment call
entries.fix: Good news on GE — the kitchen lineup (dishwashers, cooking, and fridges) is on a strong run right now and worth fixing; dryers are the weak spot (poor button design); washers are middle-of-the-road. On newer GE we read diagnostics via SmartHQ. Send a video + model # for the honest read.
entries.note: Teddy's GE take: big fan of the kitchen lineup right now (runs a GE dishwasher, would buy a GE fridge), cooking solid, dryers poor (buttons), washers meh, all-in-one not repair-friendly.

symptoms: iced up on back of freezer
entries.likely_cause: clogged / frozen defrost drain tube (backs up, refreezes, overflows into fridge or onto floor)
entries.fix: Clear and thaw the defrost drain, install drain heater/clip so it doesn't re-clog.
entries.note: THE most common fridge repair, cross-brand. Especially Samsung; also Frigidaire and GE side-by-sides; and virtually all top-freezers (ice on the bottom or water leaking into the fridge).

entries.likely_cause: sealed-system / cooling loss (low refrigerant charge, a leak, or the compressor) — after ruling out defrost / evaporator airflow
entries.fix: Confirm it's cooling loss vs a defrost/evap-fan problem first. If it's the sealed system, that's our licensed lane — we're EPA 608 Universal certified to recover, fix the leak or swap the compressor, pull a deep vacuum, and recharge it right. Most appliance repair shops won't even touch an R600a (isobutane) unit — we do. Just go with the pros.
entries.note: Soft ice cream / won't-stay-cold = the classic sealed-system tell. BRAG: EPA 608 Universal certified + we do R600a units others refuse. Always rule out defrost/evap fan before condemning the sealed system.

entries.likely_cause: Kenmore is a rebrand — the model number reveals the real manufacturer
entries.fix: Kenmore never built its own machines (Sears brand, now Lowe's) — it's an LG, Whirlpool, GE, Frigidaire, Daewoo, or other maker under a badge. Get the model number; the first 3 digits tell us who built it, then we apply that manufacturer's known failures. Older Kenmores = better built; newer could be anything.
entries.note: PREFIX DECODER (first 3 digits of the model #): 110/106/665 = Whirlpool; 796/795 = LG; 253/417/587 = Frigidaire; 363 = GE; others could be Daewoo/other. ALWAYS ask for the Kenmore model number, decode the maker, then use that brand's playbook (e.g. 796 washer won't drain = treat as LG drain pump; 110 washer shaking = Whirlpool suspension).

entries.likely_cause: failed LED light board/module (common on newer LED-lit fridges)
entries.fix: Replace the LED light module.
entries.note: Many newer fridges use LED boards that fail as a unit.

entries.likely_cause: weak oven glow-bar igniter — draws current but doesn't get hot enough to open the safety valve quickly, so gas pools then lights with a boom (or the oven never heats)
entries.fix: Replace the oven igniter (glow bar).
entries.note: Easy money. All gas stoves. The delayed-ignition boom and gas smell are the tell.

entries.likely_cause: compressor start relay / overload failing to start the compressor (usually NOT a dead compressor)
entries.fix: Test and replace the start relay/overload — cheap, fast, often brings the fridge right back.
entries.note: We love older fridges and top-freezers. The click-every-few-minutes + warm is the tell; test the relay before condemning the compressor.

entries.likely_cause: motor coupler, lid switch, or drain pump on the well-documented direct-drive platform
entries.fix: Replace the cheap sacrificial part (coupler/lid switch/pump).
entries.note: Old washers make us happy — parts are cheap and available even on 15+ year units. Almost always worth fixing.

entries.likely_cause: worn drum rollers, tired idler pulley, worn drum glides, or a bad rear bearing
entries.fix: Replace the worn rollers/idler/glides/bearing — dryer runs quiet again.
entries.note: Squeaky dryers get desqueaked. Fast, cheap, high-margin.

entries.likely_cause: restricted airflow — a clogged 4-inch vent/lint (and lint packed inside the dryer around the heat source)
entries.fix: Clean the full 4-inch vent run AND open the dryer to clear lint off the heating element / gas burner — the part vent-only crews skip. Restores drying and kills the fire risk. Clean it once a year (every 6 months for big households/pets).
entries.note: Vent-cleaning upsell hook. We do everything a vent cleaner does + open the dryer — NFPA's #1 dryer-fire factor is failure to clean the DRYER (34%), more than the vent (28%). We're C-DET (CSIA) certified. It's a no-brainer.
